examples.text: On the contrary thoſe other Paſſions, commonly denominated ſelfiſh, both produce different Sentiments in each Individual, according to his particular Situation; […]

The ſecond [blast of the trumpet] they denominate the blaſt of exanimation; when all creatures both in heaven and earth ſhall die, or be annihilated, except thoſe which God ſhall pleaſe to exempt from the common fate.
[…] in those two months, Mrs. Linton encountered and conquered the worst shock of what was denominated a brain fever.

glosses: To express in a denomination (i.e., a monetary unit).

examples.text: Oil is denominated in dollars, so changes in the strength of the dollar affect oil prices everywhere.

glosses: Having a specific name or denomination; specified in the concrete as opposed to abstract; thus, 7 feet is a denominate quantity, while 7 is mere abstract quantity or number.

examples.text: So as I take it to bee denominate of the King of the Hebrewes, which is famous with you, and no Stranger to vs. For wee haue ſome Parts of his works, which with you are loſt; Namely that Naturall Hiſtory, which hee wrote of all Plants, from the Cedar of Libanus, to the Moſſe that groweth out of the Wall; And of all things that haue Life and Motion.

glosses: A noun derived from some other noun, a denominative.

examples.text: Aristotle […] thus […] writeth: Those [words] are called denominates, which haue the appellation of a name from some other […] as from Grammar, man is called a Grammarian.

glosses: Nommer une personne dans un acte.

examples.text: Il faut dénommer toutes les parties dans un contrat, dans un arrêt.
Il n’est pas dénommé dans l’acte.
Une deuxième forme regardée par les botanistes systématiciens comme simple variété mais que nous considérons comme une espèce jordaniennne a été dénommée par Weddell, Bœhmeria nivea var. candicans.

glosses: Dar nombre o título a una persona, animal o cosa.
